scenes.headline: Three ways to make one 27B model cheaper
scenes.sub: Fewer tokens, fewer bits, and a fine-tune that changes neither.
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Dill! Three new versions of one Qwen model each promise it's cheaper to run. Here's how.

scenes.label: The idea
scenes.text: For one user, answer time is tokens times bytes read per token, divided by memory bandwidth. Each release cuts a different factor.
scenes.say: For one user, answer time is tokens, times bytes read per token, over memory bandwidth.

parts.note: tokens per answer, thinking plus reply
parts.say: N is tokens per answer, thinking included. Thinking Cap trains the model to spend fewer.
B is bytes read per token. Quantization shrinks it.

parts.note: memory bandwidth, set by the chip
parts.say: W is bandwidth, fixed by your hardware.

steps.say: Every token streams every decoder weight out of memory, once.
The LM head is read every step too.
The embedding table is just a lookup, one row per token.

steps.note: BF16: 51.25 GB per token. OrcaSAQ-2: 10.79 GB
steps.say: In sixteen-bit that's fifty-one gigabytes per token. Orca's quant reads under eleven.
Orca's quant is an ExLlama trellis code with a searched mix of bit widths.

steps.note: the only 2-bit tensors in the model
steps.say: Blocks twelve to seventeen get two-bit MLP gates.
The spare bits go to the back of the network.
Every value projection gets four bits. The average is three point two one, as claimed.

left.title: Turn effort to medium
left.say: The base model's effort dial, at medium, cuts fifty-two percent of the thinking and costs nine points.

right.title: ThinkingCap at xhigh
right.say: Thinking Cap cuts thirty-seven percent for under one point. And the two stack.

scenes.title: Under a token budget
scenes.credit: BottleCap AI blog post, Figure 3; its claims

steps.say: Cap the tokens an answer may use, and count unfinished answers as wrong.
Through the middle budgets, the shorter model gets there first.

scenes.title: Seconds per task, 16 requests at once
scenes.say: On a busy server, fewer tokens took a task from eight point nine seconds to three point seven. Four-bit weights took it to two point six.

scenes.text: Tokens and bytes multiply. For one user, bits are the bigger lever; for a full server, tokens are.
scenes.say: Tokens and bytes multiply. For one user, bits win. For a full server, tokens do.

recap: Time per answer is tokens times bytes
ThinkingCap cuts tokens; OrcaSAQ-2 cuts bytes
Hemmingway-1 changes the words, not the cost
scenes.say: Tokens times bytes. Thinking Cap cuts tokens, Orca cuts bytes, and the writing fine-tune just changes the words.
